problem: The mass density function $\lambda $ of a rectangular wooden flat plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1}$ is given by $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}y.$ What is the total mass of the plate?
worked_solution:
The mass $M$ of a plate that occupies the region $D={(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1}$ with mass density $\lambda (x,y)=6{x}^{2}y$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we express our double integral as a repeated integral:      

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-2}^{2}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{-2}^{2}6{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6y[{\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6y{[\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{2}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}6y(\frac{{2}^{3}}{3}-\frac{(-2)^{2}}{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}32y\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}32y\,\text{d}y & =[16{y}^{2}]_{0}^{1} \\  & =16\cdot ({1}^{2}-0) \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the mass of the plate is $M=16.$
